title: Some who subscribe to Dort agree here with the Molinists and Remonstrants
source_text: XXXIV. Sed & ex iis Reformatis qui Dordracenae Synodo subscribunt, nonnulli hac in parte idem sentire videntur cum Molinistis & Remonstrantibus, neque alium Dei generalem cum causis secundis concursum agnoscere, quam simultaneum, atque indifferentem, quo Deus non in causam ipsam, sed in actum ejus cum ipsa influat, quique causam secundam ad hanc, vel illam actus speciem non determinet, sed a causa secunda pro illius natura, aut etiam libertate, varie modificetur.
pass_a_gloss: But also of those Reformed who subscribe the Synod of Dort, some seem in this part to think the same with the Molinists and Remonstrants, and to acknowledge no other general concurrence of God with second causes, than a simultaneous, and indifferent one, by which God flows not into the cause itself, but into its act together with it, and which does not determine the second cause to this, or that species of act, but is variously modified by the second cause according to its nature, or even liberty.
pass_b_english: Even among the Reformed who subscribe to the Synod of Dort, some seem to agree on this point with the Molinists and the Remonstrants.

They recognize no general concurrence of God with secondary causes other than a simultaneous and indifferent one. By it God acts not on the cause itself but, together with the cause, on its act. It does not determine the secondary cause to one kind of act or another; instead the secondary cause shapes it in various ways according to its nature, or even its freedom.

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
